## Overview

This project replicates large-scale consumer product analytics: conversion funnel analysis, cohort retention modeling, DAU/MAU tracking, predictive power-user identification, and A/B experimentation design — all in R on a simulated dataset of 5,000 users.

---

## Module 1 — Data Simulation

```{r}
source("scripts/01_simulate_data.R")
```

Users are generated across 12 monthly signup cohorts with acquisition channel, device type, plan type, and age group. Funnel completion is stochastic with plan-type-conditional pass-through rates. Monthly retention follows a decaying curve with a behavioral power-user boost.

---

## Module 2 — Conversion Funnel

```{r}
source("scripts/02_funnel_analysis.R")
library(tidyverse)
```

### Funnel Visualization

```{r}
funnel <- read_csv("outputs/funnel_overall.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
funnel %>%
  mutate(step = fct_inorder(step)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = step, y = pct_of_signup)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2980b9", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_of_signup, "%")), vjust = -0.4, size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Conversion Funnel — % of Signups",
       x = NULL, y = "% of Signups") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Top Drop-off Points

```{r}
dropoffs <- read_csv("outputs/funnel_dropoffs.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(dropoffs, caption = "Funnel Drop-off by Step")
```

The three critical drop-off points are identified by step-over-step conversion loss. A +5pp intervention at the activation step is projected to produce measurable downstream conversion lift (see `outputs/funnel_improvement_projection.csv`).

### Conversion by Acquisition Channel

```{r}
funnel_ch <- read_csv("outputs/funnel_by_channel.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
funnel_ch %>%
  mutate(acquisition_channel = fct_reorder(acquisition_channel, pct_conversion)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = acquisition_channel, y = pct_conversion, fill = pct_conversion)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#27ae60", high = "#2980b9") +
  labs(title = "Conversion Rate by Acquisition Channel",
       x = NULL, y = "Conversion (%)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Module 3 — Retention Cohorts & DAU/MAU

```{r}
source("scripts/03_retention_cohorts.R")
```

### Retention Curves by Plan Type

```{r}
ret_plan <- read_csv("outputs/retention_by_plan.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ggplot(ret_plan, aes(x = months_since_signup, y = retention_rate,
                     color = plan_type, group = plan_type)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(free = "#2980b9", trial = "#f39c12", paid = "#27ae60")) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Retention by Plan Type",
       x = "Months Since Signup", y = "Retention Rate (%)", color = "Plan") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Power User vs Regular Retention

```{r}
ret_power <- read_csv("outputs/retention_by_power.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ggplot(ret_power, aes(x = months_since_signup, y = retention_rate,
                       color = segment, group = segment)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Power User" = "#8e44ad", "Regular User" = "#2980b9")) +
  labs(title = "Power User vs Regular User Retention",
       x = "Months Since Signup", y = "Retention Rate (%)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The power-user behavioral signature (high engagement completion, desktop device, referral channel) is associated with substantially higher long-term retention — validating the predictive model in Module 4.

### Month-6 Retention by Signup Cohort

```{r}
m6 <- read_csv("outputs/m6_retention_by_cohort.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
m6 %>%
  mutate(cohort_month = format(as.Date(cohort_month), "%b %Y")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = cohort_month, y = m6_retention_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#8e44ad", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(m6_retention_rate, "%")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Month-6 Retention by Signup Cohort",
       x = "Cohort", y = "M6 Retention (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

### DAU / MAU Stickiness

dau_mau <- read_csv("outputs/dau_mau_summary.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

## Module 4 — Predictive Model & Experimentation

```{r}
source("scripts/04_predictive_model.R")
```

### Power User Behavioral Signature

```{r}
feat_imp <- read_csv("outputs/power_user_feature_importance.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
feat_imp %>%
  mutate(feature = fct_reorder(feature, abs(coefficient)),
         direction = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "Increases Retention", "Decreases Retention")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = feature, y = coefficient, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increases Retention" = "#27ae60",
                               "Decreases Retention" = "#e74c3c")) +
  labs(title = "Predictors of 6-Month Retention",
       x = NULL, y = "Log-Odds Coefficient", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ret_metrics <- read_csv("outputs/retention_model_metrics.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(ret_metrics, caption = "Retention Prediction Model Metrics")
```

### A/B Experiment Results

```{r}
ab_summary <- read_csv("outputs/ab_experiment_summary.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(ab_summary, caption = "Onboarding A/B Experiment Summary")
```

The experimentation framework includes: hypothesis framing, power analysis (two-proportion z-test), metric selection (M1 retention as primary, conversion rate as guardrail), and novelty-effect correction by comparing early vs. stabilized weeks.

---

## Reproducibility

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "pROC", "shiny", "bslib", "bsicons"))

source("scripts/01_simulate_data.R")
source("scripts/02_funnel_analysis.R")
source("scripts/03_retention_cohorts.R")
source("scripts/04_predictive_model.R")

shiny::runApp("shiny/")
quarto::quarto_render("retentionanalytics_report.qmd")
```

---

## Limitations & Extensions

- Session data covers 3 months; production would use full lifecycle data.
- The power user model is trained on first-month features; real systems use streaming behavioral signals updated daily.
- No network/referral graph effects are modeled — relevant for virality-driven products.
- Revenue metrics (LTV, ARPU) are not included but are the natural next layer.
